fact_text: EEA nationals (including Norwegians) working in France may apply for a carte de séjour citoyen UE/EEE/Suisse — Toutes activités professionnelles but it is not legally mandatory. The card is issued free of charge and collected from the prefecture or sub-prefecture of the holder's domicile.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: fact_text: card available to EEA nationals working in France, not mandatory → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed that living in France requires a residence permit, so movers wait for one before doing anything else. Actually the carte de séjour is OPTIONAL for EEA nationals and free of charge — you are lawfully resident without it. Action required: do not hold up housing, banking or payroll waiting for a card you do not need.

evidence_quote: Si vous êtes Européen et venez travailler en France, vous pouvez demander un titre de séjour même si ce n'est pas obligatoire.

fact_text: To obtain the EEA worker residence card, three cumulative conditions must be met: (1) the applicant must be a European/EEA national, (2) must have their habitual residence in France, and (3) must be exercising a professional activity (salaried or self-employed) in France.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: eligibility conditions of the EEA card → EEA

evidence_quote: Pour faire cette demande, vous devez remplir les 3 conditions suivantes : Vous êtes européen. Vous avez votre résidence habituelle en France. Vous exercez une activité professionnelle (salariée ou non) en France.

fact_text: The EEA worker residence card (citoyen UE/EEE/Suisse — Toutes activités professionnelles) is issued completely free of charge. No stamp duty or administrative fee applies.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: fee attribute of the EEA card → EEA

evidence_quote: La délivrance de la carte de séjour Citoyen UE/EEE/Suisse - Toutes activités professionnelles est gratuite.

fact_text: For salaried workers on an open-ended contract (CDI), the EEA worker residence card is valid for 5 years. For fixed-term (CDD) workers it is valid for the duration of the contract plus 6 months, capped at 5 years.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: validity attribute of the EEA card → EEA

evidence_quote: La date de validité de cette carte de séjour est égale à la durée de l'activité professionnelle prévue + 6 mois. Elle ne peut pas dépasser 5 ans. Pour une activité professionnelle en CDI : à 5 ans.

fact_text: For self-employed (non-salarié) EEA nationals, the EEA worker residence card is valid for the expected duration of the professional activity plus 6 months, capped at a maximum of 5 years.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: validity attribute of the same EEA card (self-employed variant of the card, kept with its card) → EEA

evidence_quote: La date de validité de cette carte de séjour est égale à la durée de l'activité professionnelle prévue + 6 mois. Elle ne peut pas dépasser 5 ans.

fact_text: EEA nationals must apply for the French residence card exclusively online via the ANEF portal (Administration Numérique pour les Étrangers en France). Paper applications are not accepted for this category.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: where-to-apply attribute of the EEA card → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you apply for a French residence card in person at the prefecture. Actually this category is handled exclusively online through the ANEF portal and paper applications are not accepted. Action required: do not queue at a prefecture — apply on ANEF, and collect the card there only once issued.

evidence_quote: Vous devez faire votre demande sur internet : Faire une demande sur internet pour un titre de séjour, un changement de situation, un titre de voyage, une demande de naturalisation - ANEF

fact_text: Salaried EEA applicants for the residence card must provide: a valid identity card or passport; proof of domicile dated within 6 months; a digital e-photo with code; and an employment certificate (attestation d'emploi) from their employer.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: document list of the EEA card → EEA
applies_to.timing: proof of domicile must be dated within the last 6 months

evidence_quote: Pour le dépôt de votre dossier, vous devez fournir les pièces suivantes : Carte d'identité ou passeport en cours de validité, Indication concernant votre domicile datant de moins de 6 mois, e-photo, Attestation d'emploi établie par votre employeur.

fact_text: Self-employed EEA applicants for the residence card must provide: a valid identity card or passport; proof of domicile dated within 6 months; a digital e-photo; and documentary evidence of regular, effective, and lasting professional activity (e.g. RNE registration, affiliation to professional/social security bodies, invoices, contracts, sales ledgers).
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: document list of the same EEA card → EEA

fact_text: After 5 years of legal continuous residence in France, EEA nationals (including Norwegians) acquire a right to permanent residence and may apply for a permanent carte de résident or the carte de séjour permanent citoyen UE/EEE/Suisse, governed by EU Directive 2004/38/EC transposed into French law.
entity_title: Carte de séjour UE/EEE — Optional Residence Card for EEA Workers

applies_to.curation_justification: permanent-residence right of EEA nationals after 5 years → EEA

evidence_quote: Après 5 années de résidence légale et ininterrompue en France, vous obtenez un droit au séjour permanent.

fact_text: Employers wishing to hire a non-EEA foreign national as a salaried worker in France must first obtain a work authorization (autorisation de travail). Norwegian nationals, as EEA/EEE members, are explicitly exempt from this requirement.
entity_title: Work Authorization for Non-EEA Workers (France) (non-EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: fact_text: autorisation de travail required for non-EEA hires; Norwegians explicitly exempt → non-EEA
applies_to.citation_repair_note: patch proposed https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F35602/2_0, which does not carry the claim; original citation kept and the quote re-copied from it

evidence_quote: L'employeur qui souhaite embaucher un salarié étranger non européen (UE + EEE + Suisse) : en France doit préalablement obtenir une autorisation de travail.

fact_text: Norwegian nationals, as citizens of an EEA/EEE state, have the right to enter and reside in France without a visa for any duration. No long-stay visa (VLS-TS) is required. Norway is part of the Schengen Area and Norwegian passports or national identity cards are sufficient for entry.
entity_title: Entry to France — No Visa for EEA Nationals (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: fact_text: EEA citizens enter and reside without a visa → EEA

evidence_quote: Si vous êtes Européen et venez travailler en France, vous pouvez demander un titre de séjour même si ce n'est pas obligatoire.

fact_text: If a Norwegian employee is temporarily posted to France by a Norwegian employer, they may remain in the Norwegian social security system provided they hold an A1 certificate (formerly E101) issued by NAV Norway. Without the A1, French social security contributions apply from day one in France. The A1 is valid for a maximum initial posting period of 24 months under EC Regulation 883/2004 Art. 12.
entity_title: A1 Certificate — Workers Posted from Norway (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: EEA social-security coordination instrument as published → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a short posting to France leaves your Norwegian social security untouched by default. Actually without an A1 certificate from NAV, FRENCH contributions apply from your first day in France — you can end up paying into two systems for the same work. Action required: have the Norwegian employer obtain the A1 before the first French working day.
applies_to.timing: before the first day of work in France

evidence_quote: Le détachement doit être déclaré auprès de l'institution compétente de l'État habituel d'emploi* qui établit le document portable A1 "Attestation concernant la législation de sécurité sociale applicable au titulaire". Ce document atteste de la législation applicable et prouve que les cotisations de sécurité sociale n'ont pas à être versées dans l'État où est exercée l'activité professionnelle temporaire.

fact_text: All persons starting work in France are assigned a French social security number (Numéro de Sécurité Sociale / NIR). For EEA employees, this is triggered automatically when the employer files the DPAE (Déclaration Préalable À l'Embauche) with URSSAF at least 8 days before the start of work. Self-employed persons receive their NIR upon completing business registration at the Guichet unique.
entity_title: French Social Security Number (NIR) — Assignment (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: fact_text describes the automatic DPAE-triggered mechanism for EEA employees → EEA (the universal first sentence is not separable from the EEA mechanism it documents)
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you apply for a French social security number yourself. Actually for an employee it is triggered by the EMPLOYER filing the DPAE with URSSAF at least 8 days before your start date — if they file late or not at all, you have no NIR, and without a NIR there is no carte vitale and no reimbursement. Action required: confirm with HR that the DPAE has been filed before you start.
applies_to.timing: employer must file the DPAE at least 8 days before the start of work

evidence_quote: Si vous venez travailler en France pour la première fois, votre employeur demandera votre immatriculation à la sécurité sociale, formalité préalable à l'attribution d'un numéro.

fact_text: An EEA national who becomes involuntarily unemployed in France retains their right of residence beyond 3 months if they register with France Travail (formerly Pôle Emploi) and remain available for work. To maintain their carte de séjour they must provide either a certificate of incapacity, a termination/redundancy letter plus France Travail registration, or a training follow-up certificate.
entity_title: EEA Residence Right if Involuntarily Unemployed

applies_to.curation_justification: fact_text: retention of residence right by EEA nationals → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed that as an EEA national your right to live in France is unconditional. Actually if you become involuntarily unemployed, the right past three months is retained only if you REGISTER with France Travail and stay available for work — and keeping the carte de séjour needs the termination letter or a training certificate as evidence. Action required: register immediately on losing a job and keep the paperwork.
applies_to.timing: register with France Travail before the three-month mark

evidence_quote: Toutefois, même si vous n'exercez plus d'activité, vous pouvez conserver votre droit au séjour dans certaines situations, notamment : Incapacité temporaire en cas de maladie ou d'accident ; Chômage involontaire.

fact_text: Under Article 4B of the French Code Général des Impôts (CGI), a person has their fiscal domicile in France — and is subject to unlimited French income tax on worldwide income — if any one of four criteria is met: (1) their principal home (foyer) or principal place of sojourn is in France; (2) they exercise a professional activity in France whether salaried or not; or (3) the center of their economic interests is in France. A Norwegian arriving in France triggers French tax residency from the date any criterion is met.
entity_title: French Tax Domicile — CGI Article 4B (EU/EEA nationals)

applies_to.curation_justification: Art. 4B fiscal-domicile criteria apply to any person meeting them regardless of passport → universal, two records
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed French tax residency starts after 183 days. Actually Article 4B of the CGI makes you tax-resident — on WORLDWIDE income — if ANY ONE of four tests is met, including having your main home or your centre of economic interests in France. You can be French tax-resident from arrival while still being paid from Norway. Action required: establish which side taxes you before the first payslip, not at year end.

fact_text: As both France and Norway are parties to EC Regulation No. 883/2004 on the coordination of social security systems (Norway via the EEA Agreement), a worker can only be subject to the social security legislation of one member state at a time. Upon genuine relocation from Norway to France and commencement of employment or self-employment in France, the worker falls under the French social security system exclusively and must register with CPAM and URSSAF.

applies_to.curation_justification: coordination rule between EEA states, applicable via the EEA Agreement → EEA
applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can keep Norwegian cover running during the transition as a safety net. Actually Regulation 883/2004 allows only ONE country's social security to apply at a time — on a genuine relocation, France takes over and Norwegian coverage stops. Action required: do not keep paying into both, and check what lapses in Norway when it does.

evidence_quote: L'article 11 du règlement (CE) n° 883/2004 pose le principe de l'unicité de législation qui s'applique sans exception à toutes les situations.
